text:
marta: Heads-up — ran into a weird combo of issues when trying to get the JS SDK working on Deno + Bun for a small sample app. Seems like three separate footguns: module resolution (bare imports vs URL), fetch behaviour differences (keepalive / streaming), and web crypto subtlety (globalThis.crypto.subtle vs node polyfill).

jon: Oof. Can you paste the minimal example?

marta: Sure. This is what I used in Deno:

```ts
import { RedwoodClient } from 'npm:@redwood/inference'; // works in node but fails in Deno/Bun

const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('REDWOOD_KEY') });
await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood/fast-1', prompt: 'hi' });
```

marta: Deno complains about the `npm:` specifier and Bun resolves but then runtime hits `globalThis.crypto.subtle` missing or different API and the SDK throws. Also streaming responses don't arrive in Bun's `fetch` the same way as Node's `fetch` (readableStream differences).

azu: For Deno you have to ship a URL-based bundle or an ES module entrypoint like `/mod.ts`. We intentionally didn't publish a Deno single-file URL, so `npm:` won't map. Two quick workarounds: compile a Deno-friendly bundle (we have an internal script) or use the published ESM URL if you add a compat build.

sam: For crypto, the short fix is to gate on `globalThis.crypto?.subtle` and fallback to `await import('https://deno.land/std@0.188.0/crypto/mod.ts')` or the tiny polyfill we discussed in #eng-runtime. But that feels hacky for users.

jon: Streaming: Bun currently uses `Response.body.getReader()` shims differently. If the SDK assumes `res.body.pipeThrough` or standard WHATWG streaming primitives, Bun might still work but some transforms behave differently. We had an internal issue where `TextDecoderStream` wasn't present.

marta: Right. Would be nice to document an official Deno/Bun compatibility table + recommended import patterns. New users hit this on onboarding (sample app fails on first try).

azu: Agreed. I've opened a GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/412 — will add a compatibility matrix and a small `mod.deno.ts` in the next patch.

sam: Could we also make the SDK detect runtimes and export separate entrypoints in package.json like `exports.{"deno": "./dist/mod.deno.mjs", "default": "./dist/index.cjs"}` ? Node supports conditional exports but Deno ignores package.json. Still, publishing a `mod.deno.ts` at repo root (URL import) helps.

jon: Typings: another UX hit — consumers using `--lib dom` or `deno.json` tsconfig get different type errors because we currently rely on Node types for `AbortSignal` and `ReadableStream`. We should add ambient declarations for web-standard streams in our types bundle so Deno/Bun TS users don't see red.

marta: For quick unblocking, I added a tiny README snippet in the sample-app: `deno run --allow-net --allow-env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redwood-inference/samples/deno/hello.ts` that uses an explicit URL import to our deno-friendly entrypoint. That worked for me locally.

azu: Nice. CI-wise we should add a lightweight deno test (just sanity run) in our matrix. @ci-bot can we add a job?

ci-bot: CI job request noted: `deno-sanity` added to nightly matrix. Will run on next push. :robot_face:

sam: Follow-ups: (1) add `mod.deno.ts` and `mod.bun.ts` with tiny runtime detection and export wrappers, (2) add types shims for web streams/crypto in types package, (3) update sample apps and README with one-liners.

marta: Also let's include a troubleshooting blurb for the common runtime errors: `TypeError: globalThis.crypto.subtle is undefined`, `TypeError: Cannot read property 'getReader' of undefined`, and `ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_TARGET` for npm: specifiers. Short copy + copy-paste polyfill snippets.

jon: I'll take (2) types shims. azu take (1) entrypoints + docs. sam, can you own (3) samples?

sam: Yep, I'll update the samples and add a note in onboarding flow to try the Deno URL if npm install fails.

azu: Posting my rough PR later today with `mod.deno.ts` and a tiny compatibility test harness.

marta: Thanks folks — this should cut onboarding churn. I'll leave the thread open for anyone who hits new runtime quirks. :thumbsup:
